summary: Space&Sound, developed by team SynapseTrinity, is an interactive Earth Jukebox and multisensory sound lab that transforms planetary and atmospheric visualizations into real-time harmonic music. Because complex Earth science is usually experienced only through visual charts, our project addresses the challenge by combining a two-stage interactive experience: first, a low-visibility 3D orbital exploration where users navigate dark environments to recover scattered planetary data discs, and second, a live synthesizer visualizer powered by the Web Audio API that maps color spectra, brightness, and frame motion into melodic soundscapes, rhythmic pulses, and synchronized voice narration. Users can also upload their own images to hear how any visual data sounds. Space&Sound matters because it proves that space—both outer space and our living planet—can be perceived beyond sight, turning passive climate and planetary data into an intuitive, emotional auditory experience.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Space&Sound is an interactive 3D spatial sonification jukebox created by Team SynapseTrinity that transforms imagery of outer space and Earth into real-time harmonic soundscapes. Users explore a 32-bit 3D environment guided by spatial audio sensors to recover planetary data discs, listen to and download tracks in the Orbital Gallery, or upload any custom image or video into the Live Lab to hear its colors, brightness, and frame motion synthesized into music.

Benefits & Expected Impact Space and planetary science are traditionally experienced almost exclusively through visual charts and screens. Space&Sound demonstrates that both deep space and our own living planet can be perceived multisensorially—making complex atmospheric, climatic, and astronomical phenomena intuitive, engaging, and accessible for students, educators, and people with visual impairments.

Tools, Languages & Hardware/Physical Materials Used

  • Frontend & Frameworks: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Vue (Vue 3), and Tailwind CSS.
  • Image-to-Audio Conversion & Synthesis: OpenCV (to analyze pixel color distributions, luminance, and visual motion), native Web APIs (Web Audio API, Canvas API, File/Media APIs), and Tone.js (for real-time ambient synthesis and spatial theremin audio).
  • Testing & Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) for development and Vitest for automated unit and component testing.
  • Artificial Intelligence Tools: AI assistants including Gemini and Copilot were used to accelerate code debugging, explore audio-mapping algorithms, refine architecture, and structure project documentation.
  • Analog & Conceptual Tools: Pencils and paper were used extensively during the initial ideation phase to sketch 3D spatial mechanics, sound-frequency mapping diagrams, and 32-bit interface wireframes.
  • Data & Original Assets: Open-access Earth observation datasets paired with 100% original 32-bit art and procedural audio, containing zero copyrighted materials.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Instead of building a static dashboard, we merged retro pixel jukebox exploration with live scientific sonification. Our team prioritized multisensory accessibility (spatial acoustic navigation in low-visibility scenes), creative freedom (allowing anyone to sonify their own images or videos), open-source architecture, and original copyright-free assets.
